newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Rabobank opens doors in New Zealand.
newsitem.headline: Rabobank opens doors in New Zealand.

text.p: Rural lender Rabobank Nederland opened its doors in New Zealand on Wednesday after becoming the first overseas bank to receive a licence here for more than four years.
The New Zealand lending operations undertaken by Rabobank's subsidiary, Primary Industry Bank of Australia (PIBA), would in future be carried out by Rabobank New Zealand.
Jaap Klep, who has been responsible for developing Rabobank's business in the U.S. and Germany, had been appointed general manager of the local branch, effective in October.
PIBA expanded into New Zealand in 1989, specialising in rural lending. Rabobank Group, one of the world's top 50 banks with NZ$260 billion in assets, bought PIBA in 1994.

Rabobank handles 90 percent of all food and agricultural banking transactions in its home country, the Netherlands, and has a major share of the retail and business banking market there, it said. -- Wellington Newsroom (64-4-4734746)
